purpose: Design document for the start-design workflow that builds design documents from a requirements document: upstream design, matching with existing implementations, detailed design, consistency check, review and commit.
summary: Overview of the start-design orchestrator flow and its reliance on design_method
Flowchart from preparation through input gathering, upstream design, matching, detailed design, consistency check, review and finish
Preparation steps: requirement identification, feature name, output directory, temporary marker, greenfield and mode determination, state table, normative documents
Phase 1 gathers project rules only via an agent; requirements are identified from context
Phase 2 upstream design from requirements alone with approvals and design ID numbering
Phase 3 matching against existing implementations and patterns, redesign, and diff-development handling
Phases 4 to 6: detailed design, consistency check with traceability, AI and user review
Handling needs not covered by requirements: stop and report, then amend requirements or record an ADR
Completion steps and design principles: build from requirements, reuse existing components, full requirement coverage, What/How boundary
tasks: Modifying the start-design skill or its workflow
Creating a design document from a requirements document
Deciding diff-development or temporary marker handling for design documents
Reviewing design workflow consistency with design_method
Handling design needs that are missing from requirements
